outcomeNote: Mishna rulings with a tannaitic dispute.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ כְּנָסָהּ בְּגֵט קֵרֵחַ – תֵּצֵא מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה, וְכׇל הַדְּרָכִים הָאֵלּוּ בָּהּ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If a woman «was married» by her second husband «on the basis of» receiving «a bare bill of divorce,» i.e., a folded and tied bill of divorce that is missing signatures, «she» must «leave» both «this,» the first husband, «and that,» the second husband. «And all of those» previously mentioned «ways» of penalizing a woman who remarried based on the bills of divorce detailed in the earlier mishna (79b) apply «to her» in this case as well.

segments.he: גֵּט קֵרֵחַ – הַכֹּל מַשְׁלִימִין עָלָיו, דִּבְרֵי בֶּן נַנָּס. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין מַשְׁלִימִין עָלָיו אֶלָּא קְרוֹבִים, הָרְאוּיִין לְהָעִיד בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
segments.en: With regard to «a bare bill of divorce; anyone,» even those who are disqualified from bearing witness, «can complete it,» i.e., sign it in addition to the primary witnesses, so that it will not remain bare. This is «the statement of ben Nannas. Rabbi Akiva says: Not» all who are disqualified from bearing witness can «complete it. Rather, only relatives who are fit to testify in another case.» Rabbi Akiva permits only the inclusion of witnesses who would ordinarily be valid witnesses, but who are invalid here because they are relatives of either the husband and wife or the other witnesses.

segments.he: וְאֵיזֶהוּ גֵּט קֵרֵחַ? כׇּל שֶׁקְּשָׁרָיו מְרוּבִּין מֵעֵדָיו.
segments.en: «And what is a bare bill of divorce?» It is «any» bill of divorce «where» the number of «its folds» is «more than» the number of «its witnesses.» In a folded and tied bill of divorce, the bill of divorce is folded and the folds are then tied. Instead of having two witnesses sign at the bottom of the document, witnesses would sign on each tied fold. A bare bill of divorce has more folds than signatures, i.e., some folds lack signatures.

moves.summary: A woman married on a bare get leaves both husbands with all penalties.
Ben Nannas: anyone may complete a bare get.
R' Akiva: only relatives fit to testify elsewhere may complete it.
Definition: a get whose ties outnumber its witnesses.
